en.title: Cliff Booth's Rough '77 Revealed in New Fincher/Tarantino Trailer
en.summary: The second trailer for David Fincher's **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** has dropped, offering a gritty glimpse into the former stuntman's life eight years after *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*. Get ready for a darker, more grounded look at the iconic character.
en.body:
The wait is over for a more revealing look at **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth**. A brand new, red-band trailer has been unleashed by Netflix, giving fans a much more substantial preview of what David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino have cooked up for Brad Pitt's return as the enigmatic stuntman. This trailer, initially exclusive to IMAX screenings of *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*'s re-release, now offers everyone a chance to see Cliff Booth navigating a very different Hollywood landscape in 1977.

Set eight years after the events of *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*, the film finds Cliff in a less glamorous phase of his career. The trailer opens with a voiceover referencing the infamous Bruce Lee incident, which Cliff dismisses as "exaggerated a bit over the years." His days of stunt work seem to be behind him, as he's now scraping by running a movie theater, tending bar, and working concessions. However, the trailer hints at a return to his fixer roots when he receives a call from talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) about an urgent meeting. This new footage expands on the brief glimpses we saw in the first trailer, showcasing Cliff's struggles and the potential for him to get pulled back into the shadier side of the industry.

The new trailer is a masterclass in atmosphere, set to Kool & the Gang's "Hollywood Swinging." It expertly blends the era's vibrant energy with the underlying grit of Hollywood's less celebrated corners. The decision to have the trailer debut with an IMAX re-release of Tarantino's 2019 film was a smart move, immediately drawing parallels and building anticipation among fans who cherished Cliff's presence in that film. The choice of a red-band cut signals a willingness to embrace a more mature and potentially violent narrative, fitting for both Fincher's directorial style and Tarantino's penchant for unfiltered storytelling.

## Cliff Booth's New Hustle

The narrative seems to focus on Cliff's transition from the fringes of the film industry to a more hands-on, and possibly dangerous, role. The trailer emphasizes his current, less glamorous gigs, highlighting the economic realities of post-stunt work life in 1977. The introduction of Karen Crosby and her mysterious request suggests a plot that will likely involve high stakes and potentially unsavory characters. This isn't just a continuation of his past; it's a new chapter where Cliff must leverage his unique skills and experiences to survive and perhaps thrive in a changing Hollywood.

## What Fans Can Expect

For fans of **Once Upon a Time in Hollywood**, this trailer is a direct invitation to revisit a beloved character in a new context. The film promises to explore the untold stories and the less glamorous aspects of the movie business. With **David Fincher** at the helm, known for his meticulous direction and dark, compelling narratives, and **Quentin Tarantino** penning the script, the film is poised to deliver a rich, character-driven experience. The blend of Pitt's charismatic performance with Fincher's atmospheric direction and Tarantino's sharp dialogue is a potent combination that has the potential to become another cult classic.

## What's Next

**The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** is set to premiere exclusively in IMAX theaters on November 25, 2026, followed by its streaming debut on Netflix on December 23, 2026. Fans can expect a limited two-week theatrical run in IMAX before the film becomes available to a wider audience on the streaming platform.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix Cliff Booth is back, and this time the trailer isn’t holding back on the language. Netflix has released the second trailer for David Fincher’s  The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth  online, a red band cut that first played exclusively in front of the  Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood  IMAX re-release last weekend. When we  broke down the 500+ IMAX locations confirmed for the film’s global release  earlier this week, we noted that a special trailer was reportedly playing ahead of screenings of Tarantino’s 2019 film. That trailer is now available for everyone to see, and it’s easily the most revealing look at the plot we’ve had yet. It’s the second big theatrical tie-in for the film’s marketing campaign. The  first official trailer  back in September also debuted on the big screen first,  playing in front of  Resident Evil  before Netflix put it online. What does the new trailer show? Set to Kool & the Gang’s “Hollywood Swinging,” the trailer opens on Cliff waking up in June 1977 to a voiceover recounting that famous story about the stuntman who supposedly kicked Bruce Lee’s ass. Cliff’s response? “It’s been exaggerated a bit over the years.” The stunt work has dried up. Cliff is now scraping by running a theater projector, tending bar, and working concessions, while doing a few shadier deals on the side. Then comes a message on his answering machine from talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), who represents TV star Charlie Peters (Scott Caan) and wants a meeting “at your earliest convenience.” Some of this will be familiar from September’s trailer, including Cliff’s dig at his old boss: the reason he stopped working with Rick Dalton is that Rick “got too fat for me to double him anymore.” Sorry, Leo. Where this trailer goes further is in finally spelling out what Charlie actually wants. He does his own stunts, and Cliff is “too tall,” “too blonde,” and does “handsome,” so it’s not about doubling. As Charlie puts it, he’s killed plenty of people on TV, but Cliff has  actually  killed people. “This ain’t about stunt work.” From there, things escalate quickly. The axe-wielding Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena) break into a house, Charlie suddenly needs a briefcase full of cash, and Cliff is seen stuffing a body into the trunk of a yellow car. Karen is not thrilled, warning Cliff that whatever’s going on, “it’s not good.” The highlight is the closing scene.
